claim: What makes a shopfront say what it is, by ablation before a blind reviewer: the lettered name is decisive (it turned a 'dress shop' into a pawnbroker and a 'storeroom' into a grocer); a surround (reveal, fascia over the window head, pilasters between sashes) helps because the sign needs something to sit on; a lamp in the display barely matters; and goods that do not fit the trade contradict the sign.
evidence: projects/blood-city/experiments/shop-surrounds/what-if.png and before-after.png, five unlabelled sets; tests/test_whatif.py ShopSurroundTests
outdoor letter sprites per map: DukCity 38 to 73, E1M4 33, E3M1 0 (Blood leans less on signs)
use: Name first (glass.write_names on a fascia), then the surround (glass.surround, stand pilasters after the lintel pass or one pilaster repaints the jambs), then goods of the trade. Fascia lettering is not legible from across a street; cut a chain lamp to a low display.
